summary.text: A Nereid, one of the fifty daughters of Nereus the Old Man of the Sea, loved by Aeacus and mother of Phocus.
When her son Phocus was slain by his half-brothers, she sent an avenging wolf against Peleus' herds, relenting only at the intercession of her sister Thetis.

story.text: Hesiod counts Psamathe among the fifty daughters born to blameless Nereus, the Old Man of the Sea — "Psamathe of charming figure" set amid her shining sisters of the deep.
Apollodorus likewise lists her with the Nereids, the sea-daughters of Nereus and Doris.
Hesiod tells that Psamathe the fair goddess was loved by Aeacus through golden Aphrodite, and bore him Phocus.
Apollodorus gives the courtship its struggle: Aeacus lay with Psamathe, daughter of Nereus, who turned herself into a seal to escape his embraces, yet still she bore the son Phocus.

When Phocus came to grief at the hands of his half-brothers, his Nereid mother's wrath fell on Peleus. She sent a monstrous wolf to ravage his cattle along the Trachinian shore; deaf to Peleus' own entreaties, she yielded her anger only when her sister Thetis interceded for her afflicted husband, and the beast was at last turned to marble.

Apollonius records the brothers' fate plainly: the sons of Aeacus, having in their folly slain their brother Phocus, settled far from Aegina in exile — Telamon making his home on the Attic island, Peleus departing for Phthia.
